sections.heading: Glossary term: Space Telescope
sections.body: Electromagnetic radiation from space has to first pass through the Earth's atmosphere before it can be collected by ground-based telescopes. Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, and some kinds of infrared radiation are filtered out completely by the atmosphere. To observe them, astronomers use space telescopes, which are sometimes also called space observatories: Automated satellites above the atmosphere that carry a telescope and instruments, plus the equipment needed to orient the spacecraft towards a specific target, receive commands, and transmit data back to Earth. As the twinkling of stars shows, even light that passes through the atmosphere is disturbed in the process. Here, too, space telescopes can help. However, space telescopes are difficult to repair. Most space telescopes are either in Earth orbit (such as the Hubble Space Telescope), or at the so-called Lagrange point L2 (such as the James Webb Space Telescope).

Glossary term: Space Telescope

Also known as Space Observatory

Description: Electromagnetic radiation from space has to first pass through the Earth's atmosphere before it can be collected by ground-based telescopes. Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, and some kinds of infrared radiation are filtered out completely by the atmosphere. To observe them, astronomers use space telescopes, which are sometimes also called space observatories: Automated satellites above the atmosphere that carry a telescope and instruments, plus the equipment needed to orient the spacecraft towards a specific target, receive commands, and transmit data back to Earth. As the twinkling of stars shows, even light that passes through the atmosphere is disturbed in the process. Here, too, space telescopes can help. However, space telescopes are difficult to repair. Most space telescopes are either in Earth orbit (such as the Hubble Space Telescope), or at the so-called Lagrange point L2 (such as the James Webb Space Telescope).

Related Terms:

  • Infrared (IR)
  • Observatory
  • Artificial Satellite
  • Ultraviolet

See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: Электромагнитное излучение из космоса должно сначала пройти через атмосферу Земли, прежде чем его смогут собрать наземные телескопы. Гамма-лучи, рентгеновские лучи, ультрафиолетовое и некоторые виды инфракрасного излучения полностью отфильтровываются атмосферой. Для их наблюдения астрономы используют космические телескопы, которые иногда также называют космическими обсерваториями: автоматические спутники над атмосферой, несущие телескоп и инструменты, а также оборудование, необходимое для ориентации аппарата на конкретную цель, приёма команд и передачи данных обратно на Землю. Как показывает мерцание звёзд, даже свет, проходящий через атмосферу, в этом процессе искажается. Здесь тоже могут помочь космические телескопы. Однако космические телескопы трудно ремонтировать. Большинство космических телескопов находятся либо на околоземной орбите (например, космический телескоп «Хаббл»), либо в так называемой точке Лагранжа L2 (например, космический телескоп «Джеймс Уэбб»).

Related Media


Hubble Space Telescope over Earth

Caption: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope orbiting Earth. This picture was taken by astronauts on board the space shuttle Columbia, right after the Servicing Mission 3B to the space telescope itself. The telescope has an opening that allows light in (seen here on the left). The light travels through the telescope optics to the cameras and spectrographs located in the bulge at the other end of the observatory (seen here on the right). Data from these instruments is then sent back to Earth using an antenna. The black rectangles on either side of the observatory are the solar panels that provide it with power.

media.caption_en: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope orbiting Earth. This picture was taken by astronauts on board the space shuttle Columbia, right after the Servicing Mission 3B to the space telescope itself. The telescope has an opening that allows light in (seen here on the left). The light travels through the telescope optics to the cameras and spectrographs located in the bulge at the other end of the observatory (seen here on the right). Data from these instruments is then sent back to Earth using an antenna. The black rectangles on either side of the observatory are the solar panels that provide it with power.
media.caption_ru: Космический телескоп НАСА/ЕКА «Хаббл» на орбите Земли. Этот снимок был сделан астронавтами на борту шаттла «Колумбия» сразу после миссии обслуживания 3B самого космического телескопа. Телескоп имеет отверстие, через которое поступает свет (видно здесь слева). Свет проходит через оптику телескопа к камерам и спектрографам, расположенным в выпуклости на другом конце обсерватории (видно здесь справа). Данные с этих инструментов затем отправляются обратно на Землю с помощью антенны. Чёрные прямоугольники по обе стороны обсерватории — это солнечные панели, которые обеспечивают её энергией.
